what: One reconstructed human neuron: the skeleton (branch geometry and calibre) of a proofread cell of the H01 release, simplified.

provenance.dataset: H01 release: a cubic millimetre of human temporal cortex, serial-section electron microscopy, automated segmentation
provenance.citation: Shapson-Coe A, Januszewski M, Berger DR, et al. A petavoxel fragment of human cerebral cortex reconstructed at nanoscale resolution. Science 384, eadk4858 (2024). doi:10.1126/science.adk4858
provenance.licenceStatement: All released datasets are licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 License. (data page, read 2026-11-25)
provenance.collection: 104 proofread cells: 104 manually traced and proofread cells
provenance.preparation: tissue removed at surgery to reach an epileptic focus; fixed; imaged in a slab about 175 µm thick
provenance.reconstruction: automated segmentation of the electron-microscopy volume, then manual tracing and proofreading by the dataset’s authors; skeletonised by them

units.source: x, y: 32 nm voxels · z: 33 nm sections · radius: nm

frame.y: from the cell body towards the mean position of the dendrites, within the plane of the sections; used as “towards the cortical surface” for display
frame.z: across the sections (the slab’s thin direction)
frame.note: The release’s cortical-layer annotation was not used to orient the cell.

labels.how: The release’s subcompartment classes where a node carries one (codes 0, 1, 5, 3 as read from the data), carried outwards from the cell body to unlabelled nodes. Automatic labels; not verified here.

changes: converted to micrometres and rotated into the cell’s own frame
the nodes inside the cell body merged into one
each unbranched stretch simplified to within 0.18 µm (and 0.8 × that for calibre)
limits: Not precentral gyrus, not the atlas volunteer, not connected to any model cell.
No electrical model is attached to it in this studio.
The sample is a slab: branches end where they left it.
Calibre is the skeleton’s radius estimate; membrane texture is not in the data.
